_note: Verbatim findings from photo_analyses 58ac1553 (the reference bathroom). Used to (a) exercise the confirmable/confidence gates and (b) guard that the grab-bar finding stays absence-worded — the analyzer must not read the vanity's black cabinet pulls as grab bars present.

findings.title_standard: Shower Curb — Raised Threshold Blocks Wheelchair Entry
findings.finding_standard: The walk-in shower has a raised curb/threshold at the entry (visible as the dark band along the bottom of the glass enclosure). It appears to rise well above the 1/2-inch maximum allowed for a roll-in or transfer shower. A raised curb of this kind defeats wheelchair entry entirely.

No grab bars are visible on any shower wall. An accessible shower requires grab bars per §609, placed on the walls and mounted 33 to 36 inches above the floor. The framing shows the back and side walls clearly with no bars mounted.

findings.title_standard: Shower Seat — Fixed Masonry Bench in Lieu of Folding Seat
findings.finding_standard: The shower contains a fixed, solid (masonry/tiled) bench. In a standard roll-in shower, a seat must be a folding type mounted on the side wall adjacent to the controls. Seat type and height need on-site confirmation.

findings.title_standard: Water Closet — No Grab Bars Visible
findings.finding_standard: No grab bars are visible on the rear or side walls at the toilet. An accessible water closet requires a rear-wall grab bar and a side-wall grab bar. None appear present.

findings.title_standard: Lavatory — Cabinet Below Obstructs Knee/Toe Clearance
findings.finding_standard: The vanity is a closed cabinet with drawers and doors beneath the sink. A closed cabinet under the lavatory blocks the knee and toe clearance needed for a forward approach.

findings.title_standard: Turning Space — Room May Be Too Small to Maneuver
findings.finding_standard: The room is long and narrow. It is unclear whether a 60-inch turning circle fits within the clear floor area. This needs on-site measurement to confirm.

findings.title_standard: Mirror — Bottom Edge Height Needs Verification
findings.finding_standard: The large mirror above the vanity appears to have its bottom edge set fairly high. From this angle the exact height can't be measured, but it is worth verifying on-site.
